title: Volcanic soils
text: Although volcanoes are known for their destructive power, they also create some of the most fertile land on Earth. When volcanic [[ash|a]] and rock break down over time, [[they|th]] release minerals such as potassium [[and|a]] phosphorus that plants need to [[grow|gr]]. These soils also hold water [[well|we]], which helps crops survive dry [[periods|per]]. For this reason, farmers have [[settled|set]] near active volcanoes for thousands of [[years|ye]], despite the obvious danger. Regions [[around|aro]] Mount Etna in Italy, for instance, are [[famous|fam]] for their vineyards.
explanation: «volcanic ash» = ceniza volcánica (sólo 3 letras: a + 2). «need to grow»: las plantas necesitan minerales para crecer. «hold water well»: adverbio de modo. «dry periods» = periodos secos (plural). «have settled … for thousands of years»: present perfect + for. «be famous for» = ser famoso por.

title: The Silk Road
text: The Silk Road was not a single road but a network of trade routes linking China with Central Asia, the Middle East, and Europe. Although silk [[gave|ga]] the network its name, merchants traded [[many|ma]] other goods, including spices, glass, and [[paper|pa]]. Few traders traveled the entire [[distance|dist]]; instead, goods passed from one [[merchant|merc]] to another along the way. Perhaps [[more|mo]] important than the goods themselves [[were|we]] the ideas that traveled with them. Religions, [[technologies|techno]], and artistic styles [[spread|spr]] across the continent [[through|thr]] these contacts.
explanation: «gave the network its name» = dio nombre a la red. «many other goods»: contable plural. «more important than»: comparativo. Ojo a la inversión: «Perhaps more important … were the ideas»: el sujeto real es «the ideas» (plural), por eso «were». «spread» tiene la misma forma en presente y pasado. «through these contacts» = a través de.

title: Plants in hot, dry climates
text: Most plants take in carbon dioxide through tiny openings in their leaves called stomata. However, [[these|th]] openings also allow water to escape. In [[hot|h]], dry climates, this creates a serious [[problem|pro]]: a plant that opens its stomata [[to|t]] feed may lose too much water. [[Some|So]] plants, such as cacti, [[solve|so]] this by opening their stomata only [[at|a]] night, when the air is [[cooler|coo]]. They [[store|st]] the carbon dioxide and use it the [[following|foll]] day.
explanation: «these openings» retoma «tiny openings» de la primera frase. «hot, dry climates»: dos adjetivos coordinados. «to feed» = para alimentarse (infinitivo de finalidad). «solve this» = resolver este problema. «at night» (preposición fija). «cooler» = más fresco (comparativo -er). «the following day» = al día siguiente.

title: How children learn language
text: Children learn their first language with remarkable speed and little formal instruction. By the [[age|a]] of three, most children can produce [[sentences|sent]] of several words and understand [[far|f]] more than they can say. Researchers [[disagree|disa]] about how this is possible. Some argue [[that|th]] humans are born with a special [[ability|abi]] for language. Others believe that [[children|chil]] simply detect patterns in the speech [[they|th]] hear around them. Most now [[accept|acc]] that both nature and experience [[play|pl]] a role.
explanation: «By the age of three» = a los tres años. «far more» = mucho más (far intensifica comparativos). «disagree about» = no estar de acuerdo sobre; la frase siguiente presenta dos posturas. «Some argue that … Others believe that»: contraste. «play a role» = desempeñar un papel (colocación fija).

title: Continental drift
text: In 1912, Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents had once been joined in a single landmass. His [[evidence|evid]] included the matching shapes of coastlines and [[identical|iden]] fossils found on continents now separated [[by|b]] oceans. Nevertheless, most geologists [[rejected|reje]] the idea, largely because Wegener could [[not|n]] explain what force might move [[entire|ent]] continents. Only in the 1960s, [[when|wh]] studies of the ocean floor [[revealed|reve]] that new crust forms along underwater ridges, [[did|d]] his theory gain wide [[acceptance|accep]].
explanation: «identical fossils» = fósiles idénticos (pruebas). «separated by oceans»: agente de la pasiva. «Nevertheless … rejected»: el conector anuncia contraste (a pesar de las pruebas, la rechazaron). Lo más difícil: «Only in the 1960s … did his theory gain»: tras «Only + expresión de tiempo» al principio hay inversión con auxiliar «did». «gain wide acceptance» = obtener amplia aceptación.

title: Impressionism and photography
text: The invention of photography in the nineteenth century posed an unexpected challenge to painters. If a [[camera|cam]] could record a scene with perfect accuracy, [[what|wh]] purpose did realistic painting serve? Rather [[than|th]] compete with the new technology, some artists [[abandoned|aban]] precise detail altogether. The Impressionists, [[for|f]] instance, concentrated on capturing fleeting effects [[of|o]] light and atmosphere, which a photograph [[of|o]] the period could not convey. Ironically, photography [[itself|its]] influenced them: the unusual [[cropping|crop]] of some Impressionist paintings [[resembles|rese]] that of snapshots.
explanation: «what purpose did … serve?»: pregunta con «what + sustantivo». «Rather than» = en lugar de. «for instance» = por ejemplo. «photography itself» = la propia fotografía (pronombre enfático). «cropping» = encuadre/recorte. «resembles» lleva -s porque el sujeto es «the unusual cropping» (singular), no «paintings».

title: The gut microbiome
text: The human digestive system hosts trillions of microorganisms, collectively known as the gut microbiome. Far [[from|fr]] being passive passengers, these microbes [[perform|per]] functions that the body cannot carry [[out|o]] on its own, such as breaking down [[certain|cer]] fibers and producing vitamins. Recent [[research|rese]] has linked the composition of the microbiome [[to|t]] conditions ranging from obesity to depression. [[However|How]], most of these findings are correlational, [[meaning|mea]] that it remains unclear [[whether|whe]] changes in gut bacteria cause disease [[or|o]] merely accompany it.
explanation: «Far from being» = lejos de ser. «carry out» = llevar a cabo (phrasal verb). «link X to Y» = relacionar X con Y. «However» introduce la limitación. «meaning that» = lo que significa que. «whether … or» = si … o (duda entre dos opciones).

title: The Little Ice Age
text: Between roughly 1300 and 1850, much of the Northern Hemisphere experienced a period of cooler temperatures now called the Little Ice Age. Its [[causes|cau]] are still debated, but [[most|mo]] explanations point to a combination of [[reduced|red]] solar activity and a series of [[major|ma]] volcanic eruptions, whose ash [[blocked|blo]] sunlight. The consequences [[were|we]] uneven: some regions suffered repeated crop [[failures|fail]], while others were barely [[affected|affe]]. Historians caution against [[blaming|bla]] every famine of the era on climate, since political and economic factors [[mattered|matt]] as well.
explanation: «Its causes are»: plural por el verbo «are». «reduced solar activity» = menor actividad solar (participio como adjetivo). «blocked sunlight»: la ceniza bloqueó la luz. «crop failures» = malas cosechas. «barely affected» = apenas afectadas. «caution against + -ing»; «blame X on Y» = culpar a Y de X. «mattered» = importaron (pasado).

title: Epigenetics
text: Every cell in the human body contains essentially the same DNA, yet a skin cell behaves very differently from a nerve cell. The [[explanation|expla]] lies largely in epigenetics: chemical [[modifications|modifi]] that switch genes on or off [[without|wit]] altering the genetic code itself. Such [[changes|cha]] can be triggered by environmental factors, [[including|incl]] diet and stress. More controversially, [[some|so]] studies suggest that certain epigenetic marks [[may|m]] be passed from parents to [[offspring|offs]], although the extent [[to|t]] which this occurs in humans [[remains|rem]] uncertain.
explanation: «without altering»: preposición + -ing. «Such changes» retoma las modificaciones. «including diet and stress» = incluidos. «may be passed»: modal + pasiva. «offspring» = descendencia. «the extent to which» = la medida en que (estructura fija). «remains uncertain»: sujeto singular «the extent».

title: The placebo effect
text: A placebo is a treatment with no active ingredient, such as a sugar pill, yet patients who receive one often report genuine improvement. This [[phenomenon|pheno]] was once dismissed as imagination, [[but|b]] brain imaging has shown that placebos [[can|c]] trigger the release of natural painkillers. [[Interestingly|Intere]], the effect appears to depend [[on|o]] expectations: larger pills and more [[expensive|expe]] treatments tend to work better. Some [[researchers|resea]] have even found benefits when patients [[are|a]] told openly that they are taking a placebo, [[which|wh]] challenges the assumption that deception is [[essential|esse]].
explanation: «phenomenon» (singular de phenomena). «but» marca el contraste entre «imaginación» y la prueba científica. «depend on» (preposición fija). «more expensive»: comparativo de adjetivo largo, en paralelo con «larger». «are told»: pasiva en presente. «which challenges»: relativo que se refiere a toda la frase anterior. «essential» = imprescindible.
